content.content:
The registry stores each record as exactly one JSON document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`: the document is the record, the filename is the record's handle, and the records are found by scanning that directory. Form, path and discovery are one answer to one question — how a draft's record is kept and found — because each holds the other two up: one document is what a key can name, the key is the filename, and a directory of untracked state is the only thing that can enumerate them.

The document is the record itself. A record's identity is its handle, minted for the draft and written into the record as its key, so exactly one record exists per draft and the record is the thing its key picks out (owyntkvw). Storage follows that identity exactly: one document holds the whole record, and no part of a record is kept anywhere else — its state, its references and the content it carries are fields of that document, which is what lets the handle alone pick the record out. Two records cannot share a handle, because a second write under one handle names the same path; one record cannot span several documents, because then no single document would be the thing its key picks out; and a handle the directory does not name is a record that is not there. The document is one JSON object because a record is a keyed object of named fields and not a run of text — and it is not a node document: it is not `nodes/<id>.json`, it is not held to the node schema, and no listing or edge names it (owyntkvw). Which fields the object carries, and in what version, is a separate commitment; this node fixes only that the record is one such document.

The documents live in the one work-state registry under `.deccy/work/`, inside the `.deccy/` state directory and untracked with the rest of it (ulqqklzk). That place is what makes the store a directory of files rather than a change: the records are deccy's own state and not repository content, so no commit carries them, nothing about them is attributed to a change — a record is not attributed to a change at all, because attribution runs through node id (owyntkvw) — and they are not part of the tree the repository tracks. A record's address is therefore a path in the state directory and nothing more: there is no change whose ownership the file could rest on, and no node whose document the file could be.

The filename is the handle, and nothing else is. Because the handle is the key and picks the record out (owyntkvw), the path derives from the handle alone — `<handle>.json`, directly under `.deccy/work/`, with no per-draft subdirectory, no index and no second layout. A holder of a handle knows the record's path without asking anything; a holder of a node, an edit or a workspace holds references, not the key (owyntkvw), and so cannot name a record's path at all.

The records are found by scanning the directory. Nothing else can enumerate them: the documents are untracked state, so the changes the graph is read from never reach them (ulqqklzk), and a record is outside the set the graph lists and attributes, so no node, edge or change names one (owyntkvw). The directory's own contents are therefore the list of records — finding them is reading `.deccy/work/` and taking each handle-named document as that record — and finding the records that match anything other than a handle — a target node, an edit, the workspace that holds the draft — is a scan of the same directory, because those name a draft's parts by reference and no key was ever minted for them (owyntkvw). An index kept beside the documents would be a second copy of the key set, free to disagree with the documents that are the records and needing its own write on every change to state that is otherwise just files; a directory cannot disagree with itself.

Scanning finds every record that is there, and landing takes none away. A landed record is retained, not deleted (vkkwusty), so a landing leaves the store's contents exactly as they were: the open and the landed records sit in the same directory, written the same way, and a scan taken before a landing and one taken after it find the landed record still at its handle. What a caller then asks of those records — which states it wants, how many it will tolerate — is not this node's business; what is, is that discovery never rests on a record having been removed at the end where the record landed.

Discarding an open draft removes its record's document. When a draft is discarded rather than landed, its record never reaches the landed end, and the document at the path its handle gives — `.deccy/work/<handle>.json` — is removed with it. The directory shrinks by exactly that one document: every other record stays at its handle, because every other record has its own key, and no other document is rewritten or renamed. What is left is still the list of records, so a scan after the removal finds every remaining record where it was and does not find the discarded one. A removed record is absent, and absence is not a third state: `open` and `landed` still exhaust the landing question, and a record that never landed and never will is one the store no longer holds, not one in a further condition (vkkwusty). Nor does removal ever reach the landed end: a landed record is never the one removed, and nothing is taken away at landing or after it (vkkwusty). A document therefore leaves the store only at the open end — with the draft that never landed — and otherwise stays at the handle that names it.

These clauses are one commitment, not several. The one document is what the handle names, the filename is the handle, a holder of the handle needs no lookup to reach it, the untracked registry is the only place the records can be and the only thing that can list them, retention keeps a landed record at its handle, and a discarded draft's record leaves by the path its handle gives. Change any one of them — split a record across files, keep an index beside it, put the documents under a change, delete a document at landing, keep the document of a discarded draft — and the rest stop being true of the store.
content.rationale:
The registry is a place before this node: a draft's durable state lives in one work-state registry under `.deccy/work/`, inside the state directory `init` creates, and is untracked with the rest of `.deccy/` because that tracking boundary is what makes it state rather than repository content (ulqqklzk). This node takes that place and that boundary as given and adds nothing to either — the documents are in `.deccy/work/` because that is the one registry there is, and they are untracked because the directory they sit in is. Being untracked is also what forecloses the alternative shapes: a stored record cannot be a change, so it cannot be addressed as a change plus a path, and what is left is a file in the state directory.

The record is an object before this node too: a registry-local object whose identity is its own generated draft handle, minted for the draft and written into the record as its key, so exactly one record exists per draft and the record is what its key picks out; everything else it carries — exactly one target node, exactly one edit, and the workspace that holds the draft — is a reference and not identity, and it is not the document `nodes/<id>.json`, not listed with the nodes, not validated as a node and not attributed to a change (owyntkvw). Every clause about the store's shape is that object read as a storage rule. The key becomes the filename because the key is what picks the record out, so a filename that is the key gives a path per record and a path that needs no lookup. One record per draft becomes one document per handle, because a second record cannot be written under a handle the first already holds, and a record split across documents would leave no single document for its key to pick out. That the record is a keyed object of named fields is why the document is one JSON object rather than a fragment or a stream; that the record is not a node document is why it is stored under its handle rather than under `nodes/`, why the node set does not list it, and why the schema has no part in checking it — the document form is shared with the graph's documents, the node kind is not.

Discovery is the same two prerequisites read from the reading side, not a search policy chosen over alternatives. The registry is untracked state (ulqqklzk), so the change listing the graph is read through never sees these documents; a record is outside the node set and carries no change (owyntkvw), so no node, edge or change names one; the handle is the only key and an edit has none (owyntkvw), so nothing but the handle addresses a record. With the documents in that directory, the directory's contents are the only list of them, and an index beside the documents would be a copy of that list which the documents could contradict and which every write to otherwise-plain files would have to maintain. Scanning is what reading the one list there is amounts to.

Retention comes from the record's lifetime, and it is what keeps discovery whole at the landed end: a landed record is kept, not deleted, because a record deleted on landing would not be `landed` and the reversal of the recording that landed the draft needs the record to name the draft that must be restored (vkkwusty). Landing is therefore a place where nothing is taken out of the store: the directory's contents do not shrink at landing, there is no deletion there for a scan to trust, and retention is a claim about the record's state rather than a housekeeping step that might not have run.

Removal is the same lifetime read at its other end, and it is confined to that end. A discarded draft is a draft that did not land, so its record never reaches `landed` and never will; the document at its handle is removed and the record is then not in the store — absence, which is neither a third state beside `open` and `landed` nor a return from the landed end, exactly as absence at the landed end is not a state either (vkkwusty). The removal is a path operation and nothing more, because the filename is the handle: it takes the one document `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, it leaves every other document where it was since every other record has its own key, and it needs no index afterwards because what is left is still the directory's own contents, read by scanning. Landing remains a place where nothing is taken away and a landed record is never the one removed — discard names a draft that did not land, and retention holds the landed end — so the store follows the record's life at both ends: it grows and rewrites as drafts arrive and land, and at the open end it shrinks by the document of a draft that was thrown away.

Deliberately not here: the record's field set and version, and its serialization beyond being one JSON document; how a handle is generated, which belongs to minting a record rather than to storing one (owyntkvw mints it); whether `.deccy/work/` is created by `init` or on the first write; how a write is made durable or atomic and what a partial or failed write leaves behind; concurrent writers and any locking; what a listing verb reports and how a caller asks for one state rather than another; what a discard verb reports and what it does to the draft's workspace and change besides removing the document; and whether a record and the workspace it names can drift. Each of those can be decided, changed or dropped without touching what is settled here — one document per record, named by the handle, in the registry's directory, found by reading it, and removed by that path only when its draft is discarded.
